claims.statement: Poland had nearly 1.40 billion courier items in 2025, up 14.3% year over year, so monitoring two million parcels is small relative to total market flow; the report does not identify guaranteed-service or refund-eligible volume.

UPS Poland offers a refund or credit for late delivery only on certain services and destinations, subject to documentation and exclusions; the request must be made within 15 calendar days and eligible account holders can use an invoice dispute in UPS Billing Centre.
UPS Billing Centre exposes invoices and provides account roles that can view invoices and resolve claims, giving a feasible account-owner authorization model for a pilot.

UPS documents OAuth-based third-party applications linked to shipper accounts, but the public API material reviewed describes shipping, rating and tracking rather than an invoice-guarantee claim endpoint; fully automated claim submission therefore remains unproven.
FedEx Poland reinstated its guarantee on 12 February 2026 for a listed set of intercontinental time-definite services, and provides a form-based route for a late-delivery refund or adjusted invoice.

DHL's January 2025 terms narrow the refund to the time-definite premium, require notice within 14 days of shipment, and expressly prohibit the customer from permitting another party to notify claims on its behalf.

The proposed core workflow and contingency pricing already have established competitors: LateShipment.com claims automated refund filing, credit verification, broad carrier coverage and a 35% fee, while Refund Retriever publishes success-only tiers of 45-50% for smaller shipping-spend bands.

A credible first wedge is narrower than the original multi-carrier proposition: one UPS Poland account cohort using explicitly guaranteed services, account-owner-assigned permissions, invoice data and a human-supervised request step until the carrier confirms scalable automation rights.

No cited source establishes Poland/EU late-delivery refund incidence, average eligible transport charge, denial workload, or the share of the 1.40 billion courier items bought on a guaranteed service.

The 3PL integration payback, two-hour daily founder workload, PLN 60,000 capital sufficiency, 20 million monitored-parcel target and founder-net-worth path are unsupported by operating evidence or partner commitments.

Incumbent breadth across invoice errors and carriers means a defensible entrant likely needs a Poland/EU rules corpus, embedded local distribution or a materially lower-cost workflow rather than generic late-parcel detection alone.

contrary_evidence: UPS limits the guarantee to certain services and destinations, imposes documentation and exclusion tests, and requires action within 15 days.
FedEx Poland's February 2026 restoration is limited to listed time-definite intercontinental services, leaving the eligible pool materially smaller than total parcel volume.

DHL's current terms state that the customer may not permit another party to notify claims, directly blocking the assumed outsourced filing model for that carrier unless terms change or DHL grants a separate lawful route.
LateShipment.com and Refund Retriever already automate eligibility, filing and credit verification on success fees, and LateShipment.com bundles many other invoice-error checks.
The official UPS developer material reviewed does not establish a public guarantee-refund submission API, so a portal or human-in-the-loop step may remain.
